title: Mixed finite level preparation
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $A\to B\to C$ be injective local maps of complete discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ [def-pc-field-extension], and $M/L$ finite. Write $k_R=R/\mathfrak m_R$ for a residue field. Assume $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ and $\operatorname{char}(k_A)=p$. For any injective local map $R\to S$ of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $E\subseteq Q$ and finite field extension $E'/E$, let $R'$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $E'$ and $S'$ that of $S$ in $(Q\otimes_E E')_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Call $E'/E$ a weak solution if, for every maximal ideal $q$ of $S'$, its contraction $n$ in $R'$ is maximal, $R'_n,S'_q$ are discrete valuation rings, and $nS'_q=qS'_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Reduction is quotient by nilpotents; finite means finite-dimensional; local means pulling back the maximal ideal. For a finite extension $K_1/K$ put $A_1=\operatorname{IntCl}_{{K_1}}(A)$, $L_1=(L\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $M_1=(M\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and let $B_1,C_1$ be the integral closures of $B,C$ in these reduced algebras [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. A finite separable extension is totally ramified with respect to a complete DVR when its integral closure is a DVR with unchanged residue field and ramification index equal to the field degree; the ramification index $e$ is defined by $\mathfrak m_R S=\mathfrak m_S^e$. A field extension is normal if every irreducible polynomial over the base with a root in the extension splits there. If $B$ contains a primitive $p$th root of unity $\zeta$, put $w=1-\zeta$ and $P(Z)=((1+wZ)^p-1)/w^p\in L[Z]$. For a degree-$p$ extension $M/L$ of mixed characteristic, finite level means that some generator $z$ has $\xi=P(z)\in L$ and $w^p\xi\in\mathfrak m_B$. Its level is the minimum of $\max(0,-v_B(P(z)))/v_B(w)$ over such generators with $P(z)\in L$, where $v_B$ is the integer valuation taking a uniformizer to $1$ (and $v_B(0)=+\infty$). Assume $\operatorname{char}(K)=0$, $k_A$ is algebraically closed (every nonconstant polynomial has a root), and $M/L$ is Galois of degree $p$. There is a finite separable totally ramified $K_1/K$ such that either it is a weak solution for $A\to C$, or $L_1,M_1$ are fields, $A_1\to B_1$ is weakly unramified ($\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=\mathfrak m_{B_1}$), $B_1$ contains a primitive $p$th root of unity, and $M_1/L_1$ has finite level in the displayed sense [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. In the latter case its level lies in $[0,p)$; level $0$ implies $\mathfrak m_{B_1}C_1=\mathfrak m_{C_1}$.

proof.text: Normalization of a complete DVR. Let $R$ be a complete DVR with fraction field $F$, let $F'/F$ be finite and $R'$ the integral closure of $R$ in $F'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata] $R$ is Nagata, so the domain $R=R/(0)$ is N-2 and $R'$ is a finite $R$-module. As $R'$ is a domain, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] makes it local and complete, with $\mathfrak m_{R'}$ its only prime over $\mathfrak m_R$. Since $\dim R=1$ by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr] (with $D=R$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_{R'}$) makes $R'_{\mathfrak q}$ a DVR with fraction field $F'$; as $R'$ is local, every element outside $\mathfrak q$ is a unit, so $R'=R'_{\mathfrak q}$. Uniqueness: let $V\subseteq F'$ be a DVR with fraction field $F'$, containing $R$, with $\mathfrak m_V\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. Then $V$ is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], so $R'\subseteq V$, and $\mathfrak m_V\cap R'$ is a prime over $\mathfrak m_R$, hence equals $\mathfrak m_{R'}$. If $x\in V\setminus R'$, write $x=u\varpi^{-k}$ with $u\in R'^\times$, $k>0$, $\varpi$ a uniformizer of $R'$; then $x^{-1}\in\mathfrak m_{R'}\subseteq\mathfrak m_V$, contradicting $x\in V$. So $V=R'$. Applied to $B\to C$, the given $C$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $M$; in particular $C$ is integral over $B$. Consequently, by [lem-sfb-integral-element-tower-descent], for any ring $B'$ with $B\subseteq B'$ integral over $B$ inside a field $F''\supseteq M$, the integral closures of $C$, of $B$ and of $B'$ in $F''$ coincide.

proof.text: Choose a primitive $p$th root $\zeta$ in an algebraic closure of $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]: $X^p-1$ has $p$ distinct roots in characteristic zero and any nonidentity root has order $p$. Put $K_0=K(\zeta)$. It is finite separable; [lem-sfb-epp-complete-coefficient-field-arithmetic] makes it totally ramified, with unchanged algebraically closed residue field. Its normalization $A_0$ is a complete DVR by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-totally-ramified-base-change] to obtain the field $L_0=L\otimes_KK_0$ and the complete DVR $B_0=B\otimes_AA_0$, weakly unramified over $A_0$. The element $\zeta$ belongs to $A_0$ because it satisfies the monic equation $X^p-1=0$.

source.place: Preparation preceding Tag 09F4: adjoining roots of unity, with complete coefficient arithmetic.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-epp-prime-galois-scalar-algebra] to $M/L$ and $L_0/L$. Associativity identifies $M\otimes_L L_0=M\otimes_KK_0$. The algebra is reduced and either a degree-$p$ Galois field over $L_0$, or a product of $p$ copies of $L_0$. In the split case, each factor is $L_0$, receiving $M$ through its projection; by step 1 the integral closure of $C$ in it is that of $B$, which is $B_0$ by [lem-sfb-epp-totally-ramified-base-change]. Normalized base change for the original $A\to C$ is identified branchwise by [lem-sfb-epp-weak-solution-descent]. Every branch is therefore weakly unramified over $A_0$, so $K_0$ is a weak solution. Otherwise put $M_0=M\otimes_KK_0$; it is a Galois field of degree $p$ over $L_0$.

source.place: Tag 09F4, alternatives under coefficient base change; complete normalized branches.

proof.text: In the field case, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] gives $|\operatorname{Aut}_{L_0}(M_0)|=p$, and [lem-sfb-epp-prime-order-group-cyclic] makes this group cyclic. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-cyclic-kummer-generator] to choose $y$ with $M_0=L_0(y)$ and $b=y^p\in L_0$. Here $y,b\ne0$, since $[M_0:L_0]=p>1$. Let $\pi$ be a uniformizer of $A_0$, hence of $B_0$. Write $n=v_{B_0}(b)\in\mathbf Z$.

If $p\mid n$, retain $K_0$. Otherwise set $K_1=K_0(\theta)$ with $\theta^p=\pi$. The explicit algebra $A_0[X]/(X^p-\pi)$ is a DVR with uniformizer $\theta$ by [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra]. It is free of rank $p$ on $1,\theta,\ldots,\theta^{p-1}$, by division by the monic defining polynomial; inverting $\pi=\theta^p$ gives its fraction field, so $[K_1:K_0]=p$. It is separable because $X^p-\pi$ has no common root with $pX^{p-1}$ in characteristic zero. This root DVR is integral over $A_0$ (generated by $\theta$) and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], with fraction field $K_1$, so it equals the integral closure of $A_0$ in $K_1$; and [lem-sfb-epp-complete-coefficient-field-arithmetic] gives total ramification over the original $A$. By [lem-sfb-epp-totally-ramified-base-change], $L_1$ is a field and $A_1\to B_1$ remains weakly unramified. Thus $\pi$ has valuation $p$ in $B_1$, and $v_{B_1}(b)=pn$ is divisible by $p$.

source.place: Tag 09F4, second paragraph; Tag 09EV root construction.

proof.text: In the case of a further extension, apply [lem-sfb-epp-prime-galois-scalar-algebra] to $M_0/L_0$ and $L_1/L_0$. Thus $M_0\otimes_{L_0}L_1=M_0\otimes_{K_0}K_1$ is either a degree-$p$ field or a product of $p$ copies of $L_1$. In the split case each branch is $L_1$ and, by step 1, the integral closure of $C$ in it equals that of $B$, which is $B_1$ by [lem-sfb-epp-totally-ramified-base-change], so the original $K_1/K$ is a weak solution by the branchwise normalization identification of [lem-sfb-epp-weak-solution-descent]. In the field case (also when $p\mid n$ and no further extension was needed), rename the final fields $K_1,L_1,M_1$ and choose a uniformizer $\rho$ of $B_1$. The image of $y$ still generates $M_1/L_1$. Since $v_{B_1}(b)=pm$ for an integer $m$, replacing $y$ by $y/\rho^m$ gives $y^p=u\in B_1^\times$ without changing the generated field.

source.place: Tag 09F4, second paragraph: split alternative and removal of a p-divisible valuation.

proof.text: If the residue $\bar u\in k_{B_1}$ is not a $p$th power, [lem-sfb-epp-residue-nonpower-root-dvr] identifies the normalization as $B_1[y]$ and says its maximal ideal is generated by that of $B_1$. By step 1 (with $B'=B_1$, integral over $B$) this is also the integral closure $C_1$ of $C$ in $M_1$. Since $\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=\mathfrak m_{B_1}$, extension of ideals gives $\mathfrak m_{A_1}C_1=\mathfrak m_{C_1}$, the weak-solution alternative. Otherwise choose $\bar v\in k_{B_1}$ with $\bar v^p=\bar u$, and lift it to a unit $v\in B_1$; it is nonzero since $u$ is a unit. Replace $y$ by $y/v$. Now $y^p=1+d$ for $d\in\mathfrak m_{B_1}$.

source.place: Tag 09F4, third paragraph: nonpower residue or rescaling the unit.

proof.text: The primitive root $\zeta$ survives all the field embeddings. Put $w=1-\zeta$ and $z=(y-1)/w$. Since $w\ne0$, $L_1(z)=L_1(y)=M_1$. Direct substitution gives $P(z)=(y^p-1)/w^p=d/w^p\in L_1$, and hence $w^pP(z)=d\in\mathfrak m_{B_1}$. This proves finite level with the actual generator, not just a polynomial having a root. All coefficient extensions used are finite separable, and their composite is totally ramified over $A$ by [lem-sfb-epp-complete-coefficient-field-arithmetic].

Finally [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus] gives $0<v_{B_1}(w)=e_1\in\mathbf Z$. For every eligible generator set $N_z=\max(0,-v_{B_1}(P(z)))$, with $N_z=0$ when $P(z)=0$. These are nonnegative integers; their nonempty set has a minimum. For the generator in step 8, $v(w^pP(z))>0$ gives $N_z<pe_1$, so the minimum divided by $e_1$ lies in $[0,p)$. If the level is zero, some generator has $\xi=P(z)\in B_1$. Since $P$ is monic of degree $p$ and $z$ generates the degree-$p$ field, $L_1[Z]/(P(Z)-\xi)$ is $M_1$. Apply the integral-parameter clause of [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-branch-classification] with $R=B_1$, $\eta=\xi\in B_1$, and $w^p\xi\in\mathfrak m_{B_1}$, which follows from $w\in\mathfrak m_{B_1}$. Its normalized field factor is the integral closure of $B_1$ in $M_1$, which is $C_1$ by step 1, and has ramification index one, giving $\mathfrak m_{B_1}C_1=\mathfrak m_{C_1}$.
